# 玄元十子圖--趙孟頫

**ID:** KR5a0164
**Custom ID:** ZB5a0164

## Authors / Editors
- 趙孟頫 1254 - 1322
- DZJY  JY292 玄元十子圖  Xuanyuan shizi tu				:can:

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A thirteen-folio illustrated album by the great Yuán painter, calligrapher, and scholar-official Zhào Mèngfǔ 趙孟頫 (1254–1322), preserved in the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* 正統道藏 (DZ 0163 / CT 163 = TC 163), 洞真部 靈圖類. The album presents portraits with biographical notices of the **Ten Masters of the Xuányuán** (玄元十子) — the ten disciples of Lǎozǐ 老子, the *Xuányuán* 玄元 ("Mysterious Origin") — modelled on the Confucian "Ten Worthy Disciples" (*shí zhé* 十哲) of Confucius. The ten figures are: (1) [Guānyǐn zǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B0%B9%E5%96%9C) 關尹子, (2) [Wénzǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%BE%9B%E9%88%83) 文子 (the source uses 卒 *Zú* — preserved here, but a typographical slip for 辛 *Xīn*), (3) [Gēngsāng zǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BA%9A%E6%A1%91%E6%A5%9A) 庚桑子, (4) [Nán Róng zǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8D%97%E6%A6%AE%E8%B6%8E) 南榮子, (5) [Yǐn Wén zǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B0%B9%E6%96%87) 尹文子, (6) [Shì Chéng zǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A3%AB%E6%88%90%E7%B6%BA) 士成子, (7) [Cuī Qú zǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B4%94%E7%9E%BF) 崔瞿子, (8) [Bó Jǔ zǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9F%8F%E7%9F%A9) 柏矩子, (9) [Lièzǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%88%97%E7%A6%A6%E5%AF%87) 列子, and (10) [Zhuāngzǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8E%8A%E5%91%A8) 莊子. According to the colophon by Huáng Shíwēng 黃石翁 (1307), the album originally also included a portrait of Lǎozǐ. The work was commissioned by Zhào's teacher and patron Dù Dàojiān 杜道堅 ([杜道堅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%9C%E9%81%93%E5%A0%85), hào Nángǔ zǐ 南谷子, 1237–1318), and reissued in print c. 1305–1308 under the auspices of the daoshi Lù Yúnxī 路雲溪 (alias Lù Míngzhēn 路明真) of Chángchūn Lù 長春路 (in modern Jiāngsū). The printing-blocks were ultimately deposited at the Tàiqīng Gōng 太清宮 at Bózhōu 亳州 (Lǎozǐ's traditional birthplace, in Hénán), while Dù Dàojiān had the portraits copied as murals at his temple, the Zōngyáng Guān 宗陽觀.

**Abstract**

Caroline Gyss-Vermande, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 2:894–895 (§3.A.6, Sacred History and Geography), describes the album as a "fine example" of Daoist iconography in the early-Yuán literati tradition, emphasising that the prefatorial apparatus of 1305–1308 documents the printing history with unusual precision. Zhào Mèngfǔ's colophon of 1286 establishes the *terminus a quo* for the original album; the subsequent prefaces and the reissue in printed form fall in 1305–1308. The album was copied by the Yuán artist Huá Tángqīng 華唐卿 (see *Guóyún lóu shūhuà jì* 過雲樓書畫記, "Huálèi" 畫類, 2.11b), and the daoshi Sūn Dàfāng 孫大方 obtained this copy and undertook to have it printed (per Huáng Shíwēng's 1307 preface). Other works in the canon refer to the *Xuányuán shízǐ tú*, including *[DZ 702 Dàodé xuán jīng yuán zhǐ](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5c/KR5c0089)* of Dù Dàojiān and the *Tōngxuán zhēnjīng zuǎnyì* of the same author. The frontmatter brackets composition notBefore 1286 / notAfter 1308.
